visual_base.visual_narrative_log: (1) The scene starts indoors, likely an elevator or small entrance hall. A young girl with short black hair wearing a red-and-white striped t-shirt and a yellow backpack is holding a large red bag of potato chips. A man, mostly off-camera, is filming her. The lighting is bright and indoor. (2) The setting shifts to an outdoor park with lush green trees and a paved path. Two young girls, one in the striped shirt and another in a light yellow t-shirt and black shorts, walk hand-in-hand. A man with a red cap and sunglasses is partially visible in a selfie-style shot. (3) The girls run excitedly along a brick path toward a pond. They reach the edge and begin throwing pellets into the water. Several small turtles and orange koi fish swim toward the surface to eat. The background shows park benches and greenery. (4) The scene transitions to a different park area near a large traditional building with white walls and a blue roof. A young boy in a blue shirt is crouched in the grass, pointing at a small yellow and white cockatiel bird with orange cheek patches. The bird remains stationary in the grass. (5) It is now nighttime at the same plaza. A group of adults and the two girls are gathered around a dense green bush. They are using flashlights and a large cardboard box to attempt a rescue of the bird, which has flown into the foliage. (6) The rescue is successful. The woman in a beige vest and the man are now indoors in a modern apartment. The yellow cockatiel is perched on a shelf and later on the woman's shoulder. She is on a phone call while the bird chirps and grooms itself.

A light, upbeat acoustic guitar BGM starts playing immediately. (2) As the setting moves outdoors, ambient park sounds like wind rustling and distant birds are audible. The BGM remains steady. A loud percussive 'thud' SFX occurs as the girls reach the pond. (3) Sounds of water splashing and high-arousal cheers from the children accompany the feeding of the fish. The male voice narrating is bright and high-pitched. (4) The atmosphere shifts as they discover the lost bird; the BGM softens, and the tone becomes more curious and concerned. The rustle of grass is heard. (5) During the nighttime rescue, short 'whoosh' and 'click' SFX are used for transitions and emphasis. The sound of a cardboard box sliding on pavement provides a textural incidental noise. (6) In the final phase, domestic indoor room tone is present. A phone call is heard on speakerphone, featuring a distorted, emotional male voice crying with joy. The yellow cockatiel emits sharp, high-pitched chirps that cut through the mix.
